`specs/x/spec.md:7 Status "draft" does not match ...` — open that file
at that line and fix what it says. Do not install dependencies, build
the workspace, or run the suite to confirm a finding CI already made
about a specific line; a lint or status error on a markdown file needs
an editor, not `npm ci`. Run a command only when the FIX needs one: a
test you must see fail, a typecheck of a package whose code you changed.

`gradle`, `go`, `cargo` or `dotnet` is not found), do not look for it and
do not install it: fix from the verdict, push, and let CI judge the push.

When it names the failed STEP and what that step printed but no
annotation, that is the diagnosis: find that step in
`.github/workflows/` and run only that step's command. When it names
only a check, map the check name to the job that publishes it, find the
command that job runs, and run ONLY that. Reproducing the whole build to
rediscover what you have already been told costs the ticket a pod and
tells you nothing new. The pod's Bash hook refuses a test runner given

happens to be. When the report says `Ran as: npm script <script> of

(its `working-directory:`, a `cd`, or a `-w`/`--prefix` in its `run:`).
A package's test command run at the repo root is NOT that command:
`npx vitest run` there discovers every package's suite. Run 754cb4fa ran

<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="CHANGELOG.md" type="doc" relevance="1.00" tokens="186">
### Added
- **Conversation list over the WebSocket.** With `transport: {history: {enabled: true}}` — off by default, and separate from `transport.resume` — a client sends `{"type": "list_conversations"}` and is answered with one `conversation_list` frame holding its own user's conversations, newest activity first: `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, no message content. Page with `limit` (1-200) and `before`, the last row you were sent. Reconnect with a row's `sessionId` to rejoin that conversation, which needs nothing new. The frame names no user and has no field for one: the engine lists the conversations of the user your `WsAuthenticator` returned. `docs/getting-started.md` § Conversation List has the exchange.
</document>
<document source="specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.89" tokens="281">
## Asking for the list over the socket
- Serving a list is its own switch, `transport.history`, and not part of `transport.resume`: resume on with history off still refuses the frame. Rejoining hands a client back a conversation it was already in, while a list tells it what else the user has, and a deployer who agreed to the first did not thereby agree to the second ([validated by: refuses the frame with resume on but history off, since one switch is not the other @29dfea74](../../src/transport/conversationList.test.ts#L314)).
- With `history: {enabled: true, preview: true}` each row carries its conversation's opening question ([validated by: labels each conversation with its opening question where the deployer turned previews on @fea6169d](../../src/transport/conversationList.test.ts#L179)).
- A client picks a conversation by reconnecting with `?sessionId=` from a row, which session resume already authorises and replays: there is no switch frame and no second replay path ([validated by: hands a client an id it can rejoin the conversation with @ba14624c](../../src/transport/conversationList.test.ts#L538)).
</document>

pr_body: ## Why

A consumer building a UI often wants a stable, descriptive title for a conversation rather than relying solely on the first user message (which can be long, messy, or contain PII). Generating this title inside the engine is not ideal, as it would require a provider call per conversation. Providing a way for a consumer to store and retrieve a generated or hand-written title on a conversation allows them to display a clean history without overwriting the user's actual text.

## What Changed

- Added an optional `title` field to `ChatSession` and `SessionSummary`.
- Added an optional `setTitle(sessionId, title)` method to the `SessionStore` interface.
- Implemented `setTitle` in `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore`.
- Updated `MongoSessionStore.listFor` to read the title from its existing projection without any extra queries.
- Updated the WebSocket `conversation_list` frame to include the `title` in summaries, independently of the `preview` flag.
